richText: @Value can supply a configured value to a Spring bean.
The ${property.name} syntax reads a property. ${property.name:default} also supplies a default when the property is absent.

example.title: Inject an application name
explanation: Spring resolves app.name and passes Journal to the constructor.
If the required property is absent, resolving it fails.

richText: @ConfigurationProperties binds a group of settings to a Java object.
The prefix selects the property group. Binding converts supported property values to the declared Java types.
Register the class with @ConfigurationPropertiesScan or @EnableConfigurationProperties. The binding annotation alone does not register it.
Use @Validated and validation constraints when invalid values should fail startup. This needs validation support.

example.title: Bind mail settings to a record
description: Use Spring Boot 3 and Java 17. Set mail.host=localhost and mail.port=1025 in application.properties. Place each public type in its own file.
explanation: Spring binds mail.host to host and mail.port to port.
Another bean can request MailSettings through constructor injection.
This only binds custom settings. It does not create an SMTP connection or configure JavaMailSender.
